CausalChain: Elevated IL-6 → Activation of JAK2 → STAT3 phosphorylation and nuclear translocation → Upregulation of DNMT1 → Hypermethylation and suppression of p53/p21 → Increased cell survival, EMT and chemoresistance → Dual inhibition (JAK2/STAT3 + DNMT1) → Restoration of p53/p21 expression → Enhanced apoptosis and reduced metastasis
Hypothesis: Dual inhibition of the IL-6/JAK2/STAT3 pathway and DNMT1 will restore tumor suppressor function in lung cancer cells, thereby reversing IL-6 driven chemoresistance and reducing tumor growth and metastasis.
Abstract: The IL‐6/JAK2/STAT3 pathway plays a critical role in tumor progression through its regulation of inflammatory responses, cell survival, and epithelial‐mesenchymal transition. In several cancers, including lung cancer, overactivation of this cascade not only promotes tumor cell proliferation and stem cell properties but also contributes to chemoresistance by epigenetically suppressing tumor suppressor genes. In particular, activation of STAT3 can upregulate DNMT1, which in turn hypermethylates and silences key regulators such as p53 and p21. We hypothesize that a dual inhibition strategy targeting both the JAK2/STAT3 axis and DNMT1 can restore the expression of p53 and p21, leading to enhanced apoptotic responses and overcoming IL‐6 mediated resistance. This combinatorial approach could mitigate tumor progression and metastasis in lung cancer patients, offering a novel therapeutic avenue.
